description: Issue #956: neutralizes RestWidgetDataSource.FetchJsonAsync's send-time header guard by forcing the ValidateHeaders(...) rejection to never throw via a compile-preserving `false &&` prefix (same established pattern as the write-time sibling mutant). This reintroduces the send-time half of #956's defect: a REST widget fetch whose options.Headers carries too many headers, or headers whose combined name+value length exceeds the cap, is sent to the upstream server unmodified instead of being rejected before any bytes leave the process -- this is the ONLY enforcement point for a widget that was persisted before this guard existed, or whose JSON file was hand-edited to bypass the write-time check, so this mutant models exactly that residual-risk scenario. red_tests are the count-cap and size-cap send-time rejections (both non-parameterized). The hard-rejected-header-NAME DataRow test in the same class is deliberately NOT used as a red_test here: run_mutant.py's TRX parser keys results by className.methodName only (collapsing a DataRow method's multiple outcomes to whichever row's UnitTestResult is processed last), and separately, RED-verification found the 'Content-Length' row of that DataRow set stays green under THIS mutant regardless (a different, pre-existing guard -- .NET's own HttpRequestHeaders.Add restricted-header rejection, wrapped by this file's pre-existing S3 CRLF-injection try/catch -- independently produces the same InvalidOperationException for that one header name), so including any DataRow-derived name here would either be unreliable (via the TRX collapse) or, for that one name specifically, not actually detect this guard's absence at all. green_test is the Authorization+custom-header positive control, proving both that legitimate headers still reach the outgoing request and that the mutant's blast radius is the count/size checks specifically.
target_symbol: RestWidgetDataSource.FetchJsonAsync(...) -- the ValidateHeaders(options.Headers) throw guard, line ~773

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Dashboard.Rest: Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.InvalidOperationException> but no exception was thrown
Assert\.ThrowsException failed\. Expected exception type:<System\.InvalidOperationException> but no exception was thrown

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured by applying the patch manually and running exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) before writing this file, then reverting the manual patch application and letting run_mutant.py apply/run/revert it itself for the actual gate run. Both declared red tests failed with exactly this message (MSTest's own Assert.ThrowsException -- confirmed identical between Debug and Release). Also ran the full RestWidgetHeaderHardeningTests filter (20 tests: 8 hard-rejected-name DataRow send-time cases minus the excluded Content-Length row, count cap, size cap, positive control, plus the direct ValidateHeaders unit tests) under the same mutant beforehand: exactly the two declared tests failed; the 8 hard-rejected-header-NAME DataRow send-time cases ALSO went red under this mutant (confirming the guard removal has the expected broader effect) but are deliberately not declared here for the TRX-collapse reason above; the direct ValidateHeaders unit tests (which call the validator function directly, not through FetchJsonAsync) correctly stayed green, since this mutant only disables the call SITE, not the validator itself.
